title: PIO1/DMA PSRAM connected; official psram_test completes over the full 8 MiB

configuration.psram_model: picoem-devices::Psram (APS6404L 8 MiB), reused; no new model written

wire_format.finding: The firmware wire format already matched the model's expectation; this was not a source of error.
wire_format.decomposition: 40 bits write = cmd(8) + addr(24) + dummy(8), then 8 bits read
wire_format.model_expectation: Phase::ReadDummy consumes exactly one dummy byte (8 SCK) before ReadData

defects_fixed.nature: The documentation was correct and the implementation was wrong.
defects_fixed.documented_contract: Advance PIO and the GPIO/PSRAM merge one system cycle at a time, because PIO-driven SPI programs toggle SCK every 1-2 sysclks and a bulk tick_pio(consumed) followed by a single update_gpio() would let SCK/CS edges slip inside the quantum.
defects_fixed.actual_implementation: Both the fast path and the slow path advanced PIO in bulk and snapshotted GPIO once.
defects_fixed.why_it_broke: A Cortex-M0+ instruction consumes 1-3 cycles, so whenever consumed >= 2 the PSRAM saw only the final pin snapshot and lost intervening SCK edges.
symptoms: CS frames opened and closed at a plausible rate (cs_falling_count consistent with the write8 loop)
99.85% of command bytes decoded as unknown; cmd_write/cmd_fast_read plateaued after startup
Measured ~142 cycles per frame against a theoretical ~84, consistent with lost bits
PSRAM buffer stayed empty (bytes_written = 0) despite continuous traffic
defects_fixed.fix: The slow path loops per cycle (tick_pio_and_route_irqs(1) + update_gpio()) when a PIO SM is enabled, consumed > 1, and a pin-watching device is attached (Bus::has_pin_watching_device). The fast path is unchanged, so PIO-idle throughput and the no-PSRAM case are untouched.
defects_fixed.regression_test: crates/rp2040-emu/tests/psram_pio_edge_interleave.rs drives the real spi_psram_fudge program at step_quantum=8; it fails without the fix (cmd_write_count 0 vs 1) and passes with it.

defects_fixed.nature: The model drove MISO one SCK earlier than the real chip.
defects_fixed.primary_evidence: The official PIO program documents the real chip's behavior directly: 'nop side 0b10 ; Fudge factor of extra clock cycle; the PSRAM needs 1 extra for output to start appearing' (rp2040-psram/psram_spi.pio). This is the upstream driver author's observation of real silicon.
defects_fixed.why_it_broke: The model set driving_miso and popped the first data bit as soon as the eighth dummy bit arrived, so the fudge program's extra clock consumed a bit that the real chip has not yet produced.
symptoms: Read stream shifted left by exactly one bit
UART reported 'PSRAM failure at address 1 (1 != 2)' -- the stored value 1 read back as 2
Write and async-write passes were already byte-perfect over the full 8 MiB, isolating the fault to the read path
defects_fixed.fix: Psram gains an opt-in read_output_delay_sck (default 0, so existing behavior and the PicoGUS path are unchanged) that holds MISO for that many SCK after the dummy phase. picocalc-board builds its instance with a delay of 1 and quotes the upstream comment as the justification.
defects_fixed.regression_test: picoem-devices unit test comparing delay 0 vs 1 bit placement, plus a fast-read round-trip through the real fudge program in psram_pio_edge_interleave.rs (fails at delay 0 with 0x5A read back as 0xB4).

full_test_result.scope_note: The firmware's own test range was not reduced in any way; all 8/16/32/128-bit write, async-write and read passes ran over the full 8 MiB.

verify.pattern: addr & 0xFF, as written by the firmware's 8-bit pass

completion_cycles_bisected.note: At 8.4e9 the final 128-bit read line was still missing; at 8.7e9 all nine lines were present.

performance.conclusion: Execution time was never the real risk for this gate. The blockers were two correctness defects; once fixed, the full-scope test finishes about ten times inside the budget.

roadmap_gate3_conditions.condition: Run the official sample's PIO program, pins and DMA transactions as-is
roadmap_gate3_conditions.evidence: spi_psram_fudge on PIO1 at clkdiv 1.0 with CS20/SCK21/MOSI2/MISO3; DMA feeds the PIO TX FIFO exactly as the firmware sets it up. No firmware or PIO program was modified.

roadmap_gate3_conditions.condition: Establish correctness on the Serial model first and measure host runtime of the full test
roadmap_gate3_conditions.evidence: ExecutionModel::Serial throughout; full run measured at ~8.7e9 cycles and ~5.6 minutes.

roadmap_gate3_conditions.condition: Do not reduce the firmware's test range to claim a pass; only add backend optimisations proven transaction-equivalent
roadmap_gate3_conditions.evidence: No optimisation was needed and no scope was cut. All four widths and every pass ran to completion.

roadmap_gate3_conditions.condition: Acceptance: full-range test completes, zero mismatches, completion result observable on UART/LCD
roadmap_gate3_conditions.evidence: Nine UART result lines with no PSRAM failure; independent range verification 8388608 matched / 0 mismatched; unknown command decodes 0.

verification.determinism: Repeated runs produced byte-identical JSON reports and UART output.
verification.performance_regression: None. With no PSRAM attached the per-cycle path is not taken and timings matched the pre-fix build.
verification.independent_check: Sol re-ran the full 8.7e9-cycle test and the Gate 2 reproduction directly rather than relying on the implementer's report.

known_limitations: The threaded execution model has the same sub-quantum edge-loss gap in its worker loop; left untouched under the Serial-first policy and not exercised by this backend.
I2C battery and keyboard controller accesses are still unmodelled and produce errors later in the firmware; that is Gate 4's scope and does not affect the PSRAM test.
read_output_delay_sck models the real chip's access time as a whole SCK; it is a timing approximation, not a modelled tACC in nanoseconds.
RAMRD on the LCD model remains a stub returning zero (carried over from Gate 2).
